scenes.heading: Fractions, decimals and percentages
scenes.sub: Three ways to say the same amount
scenes.say: Half, zero point five, and fifty per cent. Are they different? No! They're three ways of writing exactly the same amount. Let's learn to switch between them.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Half a dollar = $0.50 = 50 cents out of 100
scenes.breaks: Money stops at cents, but decimals can go on forever, like 1/3 = 0.333…
scenes.say: Half a dollar can be said three ways: half a dollar, zero dollars fifty, or fifty cents out of every hundred. It's the same money every time. Fractions, decimals and percentages are three languages for the same number.

scenes.heading: Per cent means out of 100
scenes.say: Per cent means out of one hundred. So thirty-five per cent is thirty-five hundredths, or zero point three five. To change a percentage to a decimal, divide by one hundred. To go back, multiply by one hundred.
scenes.caption: Per cent means out of 100. So 35% is 35/100, or 0.35. To change a percentage to a decimal, divide by 100. To go back, multiply by 100.

scenes.heading: Fraction to decimal
scenes.say: Every fraction is a division. Three eighths means three divided by eight, which is zero point three seven five. Multiply by one hundred and you get thirty-seven point five per cent.
scenes.caption: Every fraction is a division. 3/8 means 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375. Multiply by 100 and you get 37.5%.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Write 45% as a fraction in simplest form and as a decimal.
scenes.say: Write forty-five per cent as a fraction and a decimal. Put it over one hundred: forty-five hundredths. Divide top and bottom by five: nine twentieths. For the decimal, divide by one hundred: zero point four five.
scenes.caption: Write 45% as a fraction and a decimal. Put it over 100: 45/100. Divide top and bottom by 5: 9/20. For the decimal, divide by 100: 0.45.

scenes.heading: Who did best?
scenes.question: Mia scored 16/25, Jack scored 65% and Lea scored 0.6. Who did best?
scenes.say: To compare, change them all to percentages. Mia's sixteen out of twenty-five is sixty-four per cent. Jack has sixty-five per cent. Lea's zero point six is sixty per cent. So Jack did best.
scenes.caption: To compare, change them all to percentages. Mia: 16/25 = 64%. Jack: 65%. Lea: 0.6 = 60%. So Jack did best.

scenes.heading: One number, three ways
scenes.say: Here is a number line from zero to one, cut into quarters. Each mark has three names. One quarter is zero point two five, which is twenty-five per cent. One half is zero point five, or fifty per cent. Three quarters is zero point seven five, or seventy-five per cent. And one whole is one hundred per cent.
scenes.caption: A number line from 0 to 1 in quarters. Each mark has three names: 1/4 = 0.25 = 25%, 1/2 = 0.5 = 50%, 3/4 = 0.75 = 75%, and 1 = 100%.

scenes.heading: Watch out
scenes.say: Watch these traps. Eight per cent is zero point zero eight, not zero point eight. Moving the point the wrong way gives three point five. And three eighths is not zero point three eight: you have to divide.
scenes.caption: Watch these traps. 8% is 0.08, not 0.8. Moving the point the wrong way gives 3.5. And 3/8 is not 0.38: you have to divide.

scenes.say: Quick recap. Per cent means out of one hundred. Percentage to decimal, divide by one hundred. Fraction to decimal, divide the top by the bottom. To compare, change everything into the same form. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: Quick recap. Per cent means out of 100. Percentage to decimal: ÷ 100. Fraction to decimal: top ÷ bottom. To compare, change everything into the same form. Now try the practice questions!
